raw: Act 5, Scene 1 — Mantua. A Street
Enter Romeo.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
If I may trust the flattering eye of sleep,
My dreams presage some joyful news at hand.
My bosom’s lord sits lightly in his throne;
And all this day an unaccustom’d spirit
Lifts me above the ground with cheerful thoughts.
I dreamt my lady came and found me dead,—
Strange dream, that gives a dead man leave to think!—
And breath’d such life with kisses in my lips,
That I reviv’d, and was an emperor.
Ah me, how sweet is love itself possess’d,
When but love’s shadows are so rich in joy.

gemma4_gloss.en: If I can trust my dreams, my dreams suggest some happy news.
My heart feels light today.
And all day long, a new feeling lifts me up with happy thoughts.
I dreamed my lady came and found me dead.
That is a strange dream.
It allows a dead man to think!
She breathed life into my lips with kisses.
Then I came back to life.
And I was an emperor.
Oh, how sweet love itself is, when even the shadows of love are so full of joy.

raw: Enter Balthasar.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
News from Verona! How now, Balthasar?
Dost thou not bring me letters from the Friar?
How doth my lady? Is my father well?
How fares my Juliet? That I ask again;
For nothing can be ill if she be well.

gemma4_gloss.en: News from Verona!
What do you say, Balthasar?
Do you not bring me letters from the monk?
How is my lady?
Is my father well?
How is my Juliet?
I ask again.
Nothing can be bad if she is well.

speaker: BALTHASAR
raw:
Then she is well, and nothing can be ill.
Her body sleeps in Capel’s monument,
And her immortal part with angels lives.
I saw her laid low in her kindred’s vault,
And presently took post to tell it you.
O pardon me for bringing these ill news,
Since you did leave it for my office, sir.

gemma4_gloss.en: Then she is well, and nothing can be ill.
Her body sleeps in the Capel family tomb.
And her immortal soul lives with angels.
I saw her laid low in her family's vault.
I immediately prepared to tell you this.
Please forgive me for bringing this bad news.
You left it to my duty to tell you, sir.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Is it even so? Then I defy you, stars!
Thou know’st my lodging. Get me ink and paper,
And hire post-horses. I will hence tonight.

gemma4_gloss.en: Is it really so?
Then I defy the stars!
You know where I am staying.
Get me ink and paper.
And hire some horses for a message.
I will leave from here tonight.

speaker: BALTHASAR
raw:
I do beseech you sir, have patience.
Your looks are pale and wild, and do import
Some misadventure.

gemma4_gloss.en: I beg you, sir, have patience.
Your face looks pale and wild.
It shows that something bad has happened.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Tush, thou art deceiv’d.
Leave me, and do the thing I bid thee do.
Hast thou no letters to me from the Friar?

gemma4_gloss.en: No, you are mistaken.
Leave me.
Do the thing I told you to do.
Do you not have any letters for me from the monk?

speaker: BALTHASAR
raw: No, my good lord.

gemma4_gloss.en: No, my good lord.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
No matter. Get thee gone,
And hire those horses. I’ll be with thee straight.

gemma4_gloss.en: It does not matter.
Go away now.
And hire those horses.
I will be with you immediately.

raw: Exit Balthasar.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Well, Juliet, I will lie with thee tonight.
Let’s see for means. O mischief thou art swift
To enter in the thoughts of desperate men.
I do remember an apothecary,—
And hereabouts he dwells,—which late I noted
In tatter’d weeds, with overwhelming brows,
Culling of simples, meagre were his looks,
Sharp misery had worn him to the bones;
And in his needy shop a tortoise hung,
An alligator stuff’d, and other skins
Of ill-shaped fishes; and about his shelves
A beggarly account of empty boxes,
Green earthen pots, bladders, and musty seeds,
Remnants of packthread, and old cakes of roses
Were thinly scatter’d, to make up a show.
Noting this penury, to myself I said,
And if a man did need a poison now,
Whose sale is present death in Mantua,
Here lives a caitiff wretch would sell it him.
O, this same thought did but forerun my need,
And this same needy man must sell it me.
As I remember, this should be the house.
Being holiday, the beggar’s shop is shut.
What, ho! Apothecary!

gemma4_gloss.en: Well, Juliet, I will lie with you tonight.
Let us find a way.
Oh, mischief is quick to enter the thoughts of desperate men.
I remember an apothecary.
He lives near here.
I saw him recently in torn clothes and with a worried face.
He was gathering simple herbs.
He looked very poor.
Hard misery had worn him to the bones.
A tortoise hung in his poor shop.
There was also a stuffed alligator.
Other skins of ugly fish were there too.
Empty boxes were on his shelves.
There were green clay pots, bladders, and musty seeds.
Remnants of packthread and old cakes of roses were scattered to make a show.
Seeing this poverty, I said to myself something.
I thought that if a man needed poison right now, this man would sell it.
The poison is available in Mantua as death.
This poor man would sell it to him.
This same thought came before my need.
This same needy man must sell it to me.
As I remember, this should be the house.
It is a holiday, so the beggar's shop is closed.
What, ho! Apothecary!

raw: Enter Apothecary.

speaker: APOTHECARY
raw: Who calls so loud?

gemma4_gloss.en: Who calls so loud?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Come hither, man. I see that thou art poor.
Hold, there is forty ducats. Let me have
A dram of poison, such soon-speeding gear
As will disperse itself through all the veins,
That the life-weary taker may fall dead,
And that the trunk may be discharg’d of breath
As violently as hasty powder fir’d
Doth hurry from the fatal cannon’s womb.

gemma4_gloss.en: Come here, man.
I see that you are poor.
Wait, here are forty ducats.
Give me a small amount of poison.
It must work quickly.
It must spread through all the veins.
The person who takes it should fall dead immediately.
Their body should stop breathing as fast as powder leaves a fatal cannon.

speaker: APOTHECARY
raw:
Such mortal drugs I have, but Mantua’s law
Is death to any he that utters them.

gemma4_gloss.en: I have such deadly drugs.
But Mantua's law says death to anyone who sells them.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Art thou so bare and full of wretchedness,
And fear’st to die? Famine is in thy cheeks,
Need and oppression starveth in thine eyes,
Contempt and beggary hangs upon thy back.
The world is not thy friend, nor the world’s law;
The world affords no law to make thee rich;
Then be not poor, but break it and take this.

gemma4_gloss.en: Are you so poor and full of misery that you are afraid to die?
Hunger is in your cheeks.
Need and oppression starve your eyes.
Contempt and poverty hang on your back.
The world is not your friend, nor is the law of the world.
The world offers no law to make you rich.
Then do not be poor. Break the law and take this.

speaker: APOTHECARY
raw: My poverty, but not my will consents.

gemma4_gloss.en: My poverty, but not my will, allows it.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I pay thy poverty, and not thy will.

gemma4_gloss.en: I pay your poverty, not your will.

speaker: APOTHECARY
raw:
Put this in any liquid thing you will
And drink it off; and, if you had the strength
Of twenty men, it would despatch you straight.

gemma4_gloss.en: Put this in any liquid.
Then drink it.
If you had the strength of twenty men, it would kill you instantly.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
There is thy gold, worse poison to men’s souls,
Doing more murder in this loathsome world
Than these poor compounds that thou mayst not sell.
I sell thee poison, thou hast sold me none.
Farewell, buy food, and get thyself in flesh.
Come, cordial and not poison, go with me
To Juliet’s grave, for there must I use thee.

gemma4_gloss.en: Here is your gold.
This gold is a worse poison to people's souls.
It causes more death in this hateful world.
These small mixtures are not enough for you to sell.
I am selling you poison.
You have sold me none.
Goodbye.
Buy some food and make yourself healthy.
Come, this is a medicine and not a poison.
Go with me to Juliet's grave.
I must use it there.

raw: Exeunt.
